environment: Humpback whale season peaks off the Queensland coast with record numbers of mums and calves resting in Hervey Bay
Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority reports encouraging coral growth on key reef sites as spring monitoring season begins
science: University of Queensland researchers make progress on a new needle free vaccine patch technology
sports: Queensland NRL sides gear up for September finals footy with Broncos and Cowboys fans buzzing
stories.overview: Hervey Bay's humpback whale nursery draws record crowds as gentle giants rest with their calves before the big swim south

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, it is Saturday the twelfth of September and mate, the sun is out and spring is properly kicking off across the Sunshine State. I'm Alex Mercer, joined as always by the effervescent Jamie. Morning Alex, and morning to all of you tuning in. We have got whales in the bay, footy finals on the horizon and some clever boffins down at UQ doing wonderful things with needles, or actually without them. Love that teaser. Grab your cuppa, settle in, because today's bulletin is full of the good stuff, no doom and gloom here, just the Bright Side of Queensland life. Let's get into it.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: First up in the green corner, it is peak whale season up in Hervey Bay and honestly it sounds like an absolute spectacle. Humpback mums are pulling into those calm waters with their brand new calves to rest up before the long swim back to Antarctica. Hervey Bay is one of the only spots in the world where whales actually stop for a break rather than just cruising past, and this year the numbers are looking strong, which is a ripper sign for the population bouncing back after decades of protection. And sticking with the ocean theme, the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority has kicked off its spring monitoring season with some genuinely encouraging coral growth on several reef sites. It is not all smooth sailing out there but every bit of good news for our reef is worth a cheer.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Right, science time. Down at the University of Queensland, researchers are chipping away at a needle free vaccine patch, basically a little sticker that delivers the goods without anyone having to squeeze their eyes shut and look away. As someone who is not a fan of needles, I am fully on board with this one. The patch technology has been in development for a while now and every step forward brings us closer to easier vaccinations, especially for kids and for folks in remote communities. Queensland brains doing good things for the whole world, that is the kind of science story we like to bring you on a Saturday morning.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, good morning everyone. It is looking like a classic spring Saturday across the south east, plenty of sunshine, light winds and top temperatures sitting in that pleasant low to mid twenties for Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast. Overnight will be crisp with clear skies, so if you are out and about this evening grab a jumper, but by lunchtime tomorrow we are back to shorts and thongs weather. Keep an eye on the western suburbs where a few high cloud bands might drift through this afternoon, nothing to worry about, just a nice bit of texture in the sky for those sunset photos. Back to you Alex and Jamie.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Footy fans, September means one thing, finals footy, and Queensland has got skin in the game. The Broncos and the Cowboys are both sharpening up for their finals campaigns and the mood around the grounds this week has been electric. There is nothing quite like September footy in this state, the barbecues are firing, the jerseys are out and everyone has got an opinion on who is peaking at the right time. Good luck to both sides, we will be cheering from the couch. Fingers crossed for a big Queensland showing this finals series, it would be a ripper way to cap off the season.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: Well that is your ParkSyde Bright Side for Saturday the twelfth of September, whales in the bay, coral bouncing back, science getting friendlier and footy finals just around the corner. Honestly what a lovely spread of stories, this is exactly why we love doing this show every day, there is always something good happening in Queensland if you know where to look. Big thanks to Sam for the weather and to all of you for tuning in this morning. Get outside, enjoy that spring sunshine, and maybe keep an eye out for a whale or two if you are near the coast. We will be back tomorrow with another bulletin full of good news from right across the Sunshine State. Until then, look after yourselves and look after each other. Catch you next time, this has been ParkSyde Bright Side, see ya.
